# Path

Native operating-system strings and filesystem paths.

## Installation

Add `Path` to the `[Dependencies]` table of your package's `Rux.toml`:

```toml
[Dependencies]
Path = { Namespace = "Rux", Version = "0.1.0" }
```

Standard packages are declared by hand: the registry does not serve them, so `rux add Rux/Path` cannot add them.

## Dependencies

- [`Allocator`](/docs/api/allocator) 0.1.0
- [`Core`](/docs/api/core) 0.1.0
- [`Memory`](/docs/api/memory) 0.1.0
- [`Text`](/docs/api/text) 0.1.0

## Guide

### What it provides

- **[`OsString`](/docs/api/path/os-string) and [`OsStringView`](/docs/api/path/os-string-view)** — text as the operating system actually stores it: arbitrary bytes on the Unix systems, arbitrary UTF-16 code units on Windows, unpaired surrogates included. Lossless by construction: whatever name the system hands over survives the round trip, whether or not it is valid text. Conversion **from** UTF-8 always succeeds; conversion **to** UTF-8 is fallible, because the system's names are under no obligation to be text.

- **[`Path`](/docs/api/path/path) and [`PathBuffer`](/docs/api/path/path-buffer)** — borrowed structure and the owning, growable buffer; component iteration where separator runs count once and an absolute path opens with an empty root component.
- **Parts and joins** — [`Parent`](/docs/api/path/path#parent), [`FileName`](/docs/api/path/path#file-name), [`Stem`](/docs/api/path/path#stem), [`Extension`](/docs/api/path/path#extension), [`Join`](/docs/api/path/path-buffer#join), and lexical [`Normalize`](/docs/api/path/path-buffer#normalize), each edge decided in writing — including that `x/..` simplification is the truth about directories and a lie about symlinks, with the filesystem-true answer deferred to canonicalization.
- **Prefixes** — the Windows family (drive, UNC share, verbatim) behind [`PrefixLength`](/docs/api/path/syntax#prefix-length), [`HasRoot`](/docs/api/path/syntax#has-root) and [`IsAbsolute`](/docs/api/path/syntax#is-absolute); the Unix systems have no prefixes, and nothing here folds case.
- **Two renderings, neither compromising** — [`OsStringView`](/docs/api/path/os-string-view), [`OsString`](/docs/api/path/os-string), [`Path`](/docs/api/path/path) and [`PathBuffer`](/docs/api/path/path-buffer) implement `Display` and `Debug`. `Display` is the name as a reader should see it, with every native unit that is not text replaced by U+FFFD: lossy on purpose, for a message, never for reopening a file. `Debug` is the name as it is, quoted, with a Unix byte outside a well-formed sequence written `\x{nn}` and a Windows code unit with no partner written `\u{xxxx}`, so nothing is lost and two different names never render alike. A precision is refused by both rather than applied, because a truncated path is a different path and may be one that exists. The exact conversions and the filesystem operations are untouched by either.

[`Path`](/docs/api/path/path) and [`OsStringView`](/docs/api/path/os-string-view) are copyable borrowed values whose receivers use `&T`. Immutable [`OsString`](/docs/api/path/os-string) has deep-copy value semantics: a language copy allocates an independent native-unit block from the same allocator. [`PathBuffer`](/docs/api/path/path-buffer) prohibits copying, transfers with `<-`, and releases its block through [`~PathBuffer`](/docs/api/path/path-buffer#destructor).

Use [`Path()`](/docs/api/path/path), [`OsStringView()`](/docs/api/path/os-string-view), `OsString(allocator)`, and `PathBuffer(allocator)` for empty values. Descriptive and fallible factories such as [`FromText`](/docs/api/path/os-string#from-text), [`FromPath`](/docs/api/path/path-buffer#from-path), [`Join`](/docs/api/path/path-buffer#join), and [`Normalize`](/docs/api/path/path-buffer#normalize) retain their names and return their value `! TextError`, as `OsStringView.ToText` returns `String ! TextError`. Raw pointers remain only for native storage and scalar output slots, where nullable or stored addresses are required.

## Index

### Types

| Name                                                          | Summary                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`OsUnit`](/docs/api/path/os-string#os-unit)                  | The unit a native string is made of: a UTF-16 code unit on Windows, and a byte on the Unix systems. |
| [`OsStringView`](/docs/api/path/os-string-view)               | A borrowed run of native units.                                                                     |
| [`OsString`](/docs/api/path/os-string)                        | Native text that owns its units.                                                                    |
| [`Path`](/docs/api/path/path)                                 | A borrowed path.                                                                                    |
| [`ComponentIterator`](/docs/api/path/path#component-iterator) | A walk over a path's segments.                                                                      |
| [`PathBuffer`](/docs/api/path/path-buffer)                    | An owning, growable path.                                                                           |
| [`PrefixKind`](/docs/api/path/syntax#prefix-kind)             | The kind of prefix a path opens with.                                                               |

### Functions

| Name                                                              | Summary                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`IsSeparator`](/docs/api/path/syntax#is-separator)               | Whether `unit` separates path segments on this system.                                                                                                                          |
| [`PreferredSeparator`](/docs/api/path/syntax#preferred-separator) | The separator this system prefers when one has to be written.                                                                                                                   |
| [`Join`](/docs/api/path/path-buffer#join)                         | A fresh buffer holding `base` with `segment` pushed onto it.                                                                                                                    |
| [`Normalize`](/docs/api/path/path-buffer#normalize)               | A fresh buffer holding `path` lexically simplified: separator runs collapsed to the preferred separator, `.` segments dropped, and `..` resolved against the segment before it. |
| [`PrefixLength`](/docs/api/path/syntax#prefix-length)             | How many units of `path` are prefix, and which kind, reported through `kind`.                                                                                                   |
| [`HasRoot`](/docs/api/path/syntax#has-root)                       | Whether `path` has a root: a separator standing where the segments begin.                                                                                                       |
| [`IsAbsolute`](/docs/api/path/syntax#is-absolute)                 | Whether `path` names one place regardless of any current directory.                                                                                                             |
